# BikeNetKit

> The digital toolkit for bicycle networks. Free, open-source Python tools for designing
> well-connected bicycle infrastructure, with interactive visualizations for cities worldwide.
> Audience: policy makers, sustainable-mobility advocates, and city/transport planners.

BikeNetKit turns a decade of research on the *Science of Bicycle Networks* into user-friendly
decision-support tools for urban planners and proactive citizens. The site at
https://bikenetkit.org showcases each tool and lets you explore its output on real cities on an
interactive map (metric, network type, and city are chosen through the URL). The code is licensed
under the GNU AGPL-3.0.

## Interactive tools

- [GrowBikeNet](https://bikenetkit.org/growbikenet): Extend a bicycle network or grow one from scratch. Paper: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-022-10783-y — Code: https://github.com/BikeNetKit/GrowBikeNet
- [FixBikeNet](https://bikenetkit.org/fixbikenet): Find the missing links in bicycle networks. Paper: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1111/gean.12324 — Code: https://github.com/BikeNetKit/FixBikeNet
- [LinkBikeNet](https://bikenetkit.org/linkbikenet): Connect fragmented bicycle network pieces. Paper: https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsos.201130 — Code: https://github.com/BikeNetKit/LinkBikeNet
- [superblockify](https://bikenetkit.org/superblockify): Create calmer neighborhoods while keeping through-traffic on suitable roads. Paper: https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.06798 — Code: https://github.com/BikeNetKit/superblockify
- [SortBikeNet](https://bikenetkit.org/sortbikenet): Find the best implementation of a bicycle network plan — the order in which to build it. Covers one city, Paris, comparing eleven build orderings (including the order Paris actually built) from three starting points. Code: https://github.com/BikeNetKit/SortBikeNet

## More tools

Seven further tools, collected on one page at https://bikenetkit.org/more-tools — each anchored
at its own section rather than a page of its own. Only BikeNetLib is part of BikeNetKit; the rest
are related work by the same research community, listed because they solve adjacent problems.

### Part of BikeNetKit

- [BikeNetLib](https://bikenetkit.org/more-tools#bikenetlib): The shared Python toolkit that powers the rest of the BikeNetKit family. Code: https://github.com/BikeNetKit/BikeNetLib

### Related tools

- [MoveBikeNet](https://bikenetkit.org/more-tools#movebikenet): Trace how cyclists actually move, to reveal the routes they want rather than the ones they are given. Paper: https://findingspress.org/article/56683-computational-desire-line-analysis-of-cyclists-on-the-dybbolsbro-intersection-in-copenhagen
- [BikeDNA](https://bikenetkit.org/more-tools#bikedna): Assess the quality of bicycle infrastructure data by comparing OSM against reference datasets. Paper: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/23998083231184471
- [HoodBikeNet](https://bikenetkit.org/more-tools#hoodbikenet): Grow the network neighborhood by neighborhood, linking low-traffic areas into one safe cycling web.
- [StretchBikeNet](https://bikenetkit.org/more-tools#stretchbikenet): Find the corridors worth stretching and upgrading, using optimal transport across a multilayer city network. Paper: https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsif.2024.0532 — Code: https://github.com/cdebacco/MultiOT
- [BikeNodePlanner](https://bikenetkit.org/more-tools#bikenodeplanner): Evaluate a planned bicycle node network against the terrain, services and destinations around it. Paper: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/23998083251355999 — Code: https://github.com/anastassiavybornova/bike-node-planner
- [LoopBikeNet](https://bikenetkit.org/more-tools#loopbikenet): Take a census of the loops a node network offers, to see which round trips it actually makes possible. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07029 — Code: https://github.com/mszell/bikenwloops

## Full reference

- [llms-full.txt](https://bikenetkit.org/llms-full.txt): every interactive tool in full — what it computes, each option on its map, how the headline number is derived, coverage, papers and code. Generated from the site's own copy.

## Explore by city

- [Cities](https://bikenetkit.org/cities): browse every covered city.
- [Tool coverage table](https://bikenetkit.org/cities/table): cities × tools, with recommended and available datasets, each linking to its map.
